solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English doctor arranged doses with superior effect? (8)

indicators.note: the letters of DOSES are put in a new order

blocks.note: MB = Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

annotation.surface: An English physician boasts that his rearranged prescription works a treat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Superior' is literal here: embossed lettering stands up above the surface, so the effect is superior in the sense of higher.
annotation.definitionFit: Embossed work is raised, giving its design a higher or superior position on the page.

clue.text: Duty shown by former monarch disembarking from train (6)

indicators.note: ER gets off, leaving the word it rode in

blocks.note: ER = Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen; removed from EXERCISE

annotation.surface: A tax revealed when an old king steps down off a railway carriage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Train' pulls towards railways, but it is the verb: to train is to exercise, and taking ER out of EXERCISE leaves the duty.
annotation.definitionFit: Excise is a duty charged on goods produced or sold at home.

clue.text: Puzzle busy person about rising total (6)

indicators.note: BEE goes round the other piece
in a down clue, SUM read upwards comes out MUS

blocks.note: as busy as a bee; split around the total
sum = total, turned upwards to MUS

annotation.surface: A harried worker is baffled by a figure that keeps going up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Busy person' is a crossword stock phrase for a bee, the proverbially busy insect.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bemusing someone leaves them puzzled, so the verb serves for puzzle.

clue.text: New toaster in shop (9)

definitions.note: stationer names the trader; in British usage it also stands for the shop, as in 'the stationer's'

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new

annotation.surface: A brand-new kitchen toaster is on display in a store.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'in shop' to say where the toaster is; 'in' is fodder and 'shop' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A stationer sells paper, pens and envelopes, so the name serves for the shop itself.

clue.text: Urges monk to avoid popular English breakfast dish? (4,8)

indicators.note: the monk's name leaves out IN and E

blocks.note: a Benedictine is a monk of St Benedict's order

annotation.surface: Someone presses a monk to steer clear of the well-loved full English fry-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'English breakfast' reads as one phrase; split it, since 'English' is a letter the monk loses and 'breakfast dish' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict, poached eggs and ham on a muffin with hollandaise, is a classic breakfast or brunch dish.

clue.text: Argument about Arabic customs duty (6)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the argument wraps around the abbreviation

blocks.note: a tiff = a minor argument; split around AR

annotation.surface: A row breaks out over what traders in the Arab world must pay.
annotation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax on imports or exports.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arabic' is not a people here but its dictionary abbreviation, Ar, tucked inside the quarrel.

clue.text: A good mimic offering astonished expression (5)

blocks.note: an ape = a mimic, one who apes

annotation.surface: A skilled impressionist pulls a face of utter amazement.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone agape stands with mouth wide open, the look of astonishment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mimic' is the noun: an ape, the animal proverbial for copying.

clue.text: Ship Inn has a girl turning up inside (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, MAID read upwards gives DIAM
the reversed A MAID goes within INN

blocks.note: as printed; split around the rest
a maid = a girl; turned up to DIAMA

annotation.surface: The Ship, a pub, has a young woman arriving to work behind the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ship Inn' looks like a pub name, but 'Ship' is the definition and 'Inn' is the container. An Indiaman was a large trading vessel sailing to India.
annotation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a sailing ship in the India trade, such as those of the East India Company.

clue.text: Endless membrane, I concur, is lacking a lacy structure (8)

indicators.note: FILM loses its last letter
I AGREE goes without its A

blocks.note: a film is a thin membrane; drop the end, FIL
removed from I AGREE, leaving IGREE

annotation.surface: Someone agrees that a torn skin is missing its fine lace-like pattern.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface, but only one is needed: 'lacking a' removes A, and the definition is 'a lacy structure'.
annotation.definitionFit: Filigree is delicate ornamental work of fine wire or thread, lacelike in form.

clue.text: Cold morning: difficult job hosting Government’s first initiative (8)

indicators.note: a host has a guest inside the house, so PAIN holds G within it
only the first letter of Government is used

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
a pain = a difficult job; split around G

annotation.surface: On a chilly morning, a tough task lands the government's new policy launch.
annotation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised initiative towards a goal.
annotation.walkthrough: A difficult job is a pain; 'Government's first' supplies only its opening letter.

clue.text: Shoe sale’s opening with everything reduced (6)

indicators.note: only the first letter of sale is used
ALL is cut short by a letter

annotation.surface: A footwear sale launches with every item marked down.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the sandal is one kind of shoe, open with straps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' sounds like a sale price, but it clips the last letter off ALL.

clue.text: Be involved with grisly tome of a romantic nature (3-5-4)

indicators.note: BE is tangled up with the other letters

annotation.surface: Someone is urged to get caught up in a gruesome big book.
annotation.walkthrough: A grisly tome is the opposite of a love story, which is what hides the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Boy-meets-girl describes a conventional romantic story, used as an adjective as in 'a boy-meets-girl film'.

clue.text: Discover that man wants minute dish from Japan (5)

indicators.note: 'wants' in its old sense of lacks, as in 'found wanting', so HIM goes without M

blocks.note: to sus (or suss) out = to discover

annotation.surface: Someone finds out that a fellow needs a tiny Japanese meal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wants' means lacks, not desires; and 'minute' is the time unit M, not tiny. SUS is a recognised spelling of SUSS.
annotation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish and other toppings.

clue.text: Backfire managed to be suppressed by thunder for example (9)

indicators.note: RAN is held down inside BOOM and EG

blocks.note: e.g. = for example; split around RAN

annotation.surface: A failed scheme is drowned out by a noise like thunder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thunder for example' reads as one idea, but the example marker is its own piece, not a description of thunder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plan that boomerangs comes back to hurt its maker, so it backfires.

clue.text: Man worked with don, I bet? Definitely (3,2,7)

indicators.note: MAN is worked into a new order along with DON I

annotation.surface: A man collaborated with a university lecturer, and the speaker wagers that's certain.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the wordplay and 'Definitely' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: 'And no mistake' is an emphatic tag meaning certainly, definitely.

clue.text: Best pedalo’s left out at sea for something better? (9)

indicators.note: 'left' supplies L and 'out' says it is dropped from the fodder
the remaining letters are thrown into confusion

annotation.surface: A top pleasure-pedal boat is abandoned on the water in favour of an upgrade.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: a speedboat is something better than a pedalo, and the surface is already on the water.
annotation.definitionFit: Compared with a pedalo, a speedboat is a clear upgrade, hence something better.

clue.text: University student taken on by a hat company in Mexican city (8)

indicators.note: A CAP CO takes U and L on board

annotation.surface: A college student is hired by a milliner in Mexico.
annotation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort city on the Pacific coast of Mexico.
annotation.walkthrough: L for student comes from the L-plate a learner driver displays in Britain.

clue.text: Tidal flood in sea that’s shrinking due to trees? (8)

indicators.note: 'in' places the tidal flood inside the sea

blocks.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia has shrunk drastically; split around BORE
a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river

annotation.surface: A surge of tide pours into a dwindling sea, perhaps because of forests.
annotation.walkthrough: The Aral Sea, between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, is famous for having shrunk to a fraction of its size.
annotation.definitionFit: Arboreal means relating to trees, which the clue gives loosely as 'due to trees'.

clue.text: Writer’s trip by wagon taking in grand prison like Alcatraz? (9,3)

indicators.note: to take in is to admit someone inside, so the cart ride admits G

blocks.note: a cart ride; split around G
pen, short for penitentiary, a US prison like Alcatraz

annotation.surface: An author travels by wagon to a notorious island jail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author, but it is the instrument. The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A cartridge pen is a fountain pen fed by a replaceable ink cartridge, a writing instrument.

clue.text: I’m ready to wear knockout Oriental gear (6)

indicators.note: KO puts on IMON, surrounding it

annotation.surface: A boxer announces they are prepared to put on Eastern fighting kit.
annotation.definitionFit: A kimono is the traditional robe of Japan.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I'm on' is the performer's cue: ready to go.

clue.text: Gutsy fellow that is upset over messy situation (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, IE is turned upside down to EI
these pieces sit above STY

blocks.note: i.e. = that is; turned to EI
a sty (pigsty) is a filthy mess

annotation.surface: A plucky man gets upset about the chaos around him.
annotation.definitionFit: Feisty means spirited and courageous, gutsy.
annotation.walkthrough: A sty is a pigsty, the standard image of a mess.

clue.text: Trunk for captain going round Channel Islands (9)

indicators.note: 'going round' means encircling, so BOSS surrounds CI

blocks.note: the captain is the boss; split around CI

annotation.surface: A luggage trunk is packed for a skipper sailing around Jersey and Guernsey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' looks like luggage or a tree, but it is the elephant's nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A proboscis is an elongated nose or snout, such as an elephant's trunk.

clue.text: Old article about church is deep (5)

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the article surrounds the church

blocks.note: an is an indefinite article; split around CE

annotation.surface: An ancient text on the church is profound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deep' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun: the deep is the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: 'The deep' is a literary noun for the sea, so deep stands for ocean.

clue.text: Press locating Republican in sleazy bar (5)

indicators.note: 'locating' means setting in a place, and the place is given by 'in'
'in' places R inside the sleazy bar

blocks.note: a dive is a seedy bar; split around R

annotation.surface: Journalists track down a Republican politician in a seedy nightspot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists, but it is the verb: to press is to drive forward.
annotation.definitionFit: To press or drive is to push forward with force, as in pressing or driving home an attack.

clue.text: Story presented by the German songs in recitals (6)

blocks.note: a story = a lie, a fib

annotation.surface: A tale told by a German, set to music at a concert.
annotation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, the staple of the vocal recital.
annotation.walkthrough: Lieder is German for songs; the word is used in English for German art songs sung in recitals.

clue.text: Fail to return a lot of anger, lacking courage (8)

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so OMIT runs backwards
most of ROUSE, losing its last letter

blocks.note: to omit = to fail (to do); reversed to TIMO
to rouse = to anger, stir up; cut to ROUS

annotation.surface: A coward can't give back most of the fury aimed at them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fail to return' wants to be one idea; split it, OMIT and a reversal indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a timorous person is fearful and so lacks courage.

clue.text: Disruption to El Nino connected to Internet (6)

indicators.note: the letters of EL NINO are thrown out of order

annotation.surface: The El Niño weather pattern knocks out the web connection.
annotation.definitionFit: A computing term: a device or user online has a live connection to the Internet.
annotation.walkthrough: El Niño is the Pacific weather pattern; its tilde vanishes and the six letters rearrange.

clue.text: Line adopted in instinctive, fashionable sin (8)

indicators.note: to be adopted in is to be taken into a family, so L is taken into GUT

blocks.note: a gut reaction is instinctive; split around L

annotation.surface: A party line taken up by trendy people who sin without thinking.
annotation.definitionFit: Gluttony is one of the seven deadly sins.
annotation.walkthrough: Tony, meaning stylish or upmarket, is from 'tone', as in a place with tone.
